title: Interchanged Columns and Rows

illustrates.quote: Wide Tables: Interchanged Columns and Rows. Sometimes it is possible to fit a wide table across the page by interchanging the table columns and rows. This is done only if it preserves the clarity of the table. Insert a transcriber's note before the table. Sample: Columns and rows are interchanged. (See Sample 11-23: Interchanged Columns and Rows on page 11-49.)

print.notes: In print, the six months are columns and Sunrise/Sunset are the two rows; the braille transcription swaps this so months become row headings and Sunrise/Sunset become the (only two) column headings, letting six data rows replace six wide columns.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box; two-row (Sunrise/Sunset), six-column (Jan-Jun) layout; header row (months) bold.

braille.notes: Line 1 placeholder 'text'. A transcriber's note on line 4 states, in substance, that columns and rows are interchanged - matching the rule's sample sentence exactly. The table body (lines 6-13) then has Sunrise/Sunset as the two column headings and Jan/Feb/Mar/Apr/May/Jun as the six row headings - the inverse orientation of the print original.

resolution: print.headers' first cell resolved to '' (blank above the Sunrise/Sunset row headings in print), not a fabricated '(row)' placeholder; confirmed against the PDF image (p. 331).
